This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest.
2.

The petition averments briefly stated as under; That on 20.12.2023 at about 4.10 p.m. petitioner was riding a Scooty bearing Reg. No.KA-35-EN-9779 near Thoranagal 1st Railway Gate, Sandur,
Ballari District, at that time, a Innova Car bearing Reg. No.KA-22-AA-2238 SCCH-5 came at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed violently against the petitioner's scooty, as a result of which, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous head injury.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Sanjeevini Hospital, Sandur, after first aid shifted to Ballari Trauma Care, thereafter shifted to Fortis Hospital, Bengaluru.

Further petitioner has spent an amount of Rs.5,00,000/-
towards treatment, medicine, conveyance etc.,
3.
At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 64 years, hale and healthy, working as agriculturist, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the accident, petitioner is bedridden and lost his earnings and in future he cannot do agricultural work or any other avocation.
With regard to accident crime No.198/2023 is registered against the driver of the offending vehicle SCCH-5 before the Thoranagal P.S. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has not appeared before court hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

Further submitted issuance of Passenger Carrying - 4 Wheeler Package Policy bearing No.OG-24-1701-1803-00001948 in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-22-AA-2238 and it is valid from 25.04.2023 to 24.04.2024 and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Respondent No.1 submitted that, SCCH-5 there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties as the owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EN-9779 are not made as parties to the proceedings.
Further submitted that, driver of the offending vehicle did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Respondent No.2 denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. Based on the pleadings of the parties this court has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 20.12.2023 at about 1.10 p.m. near Thorangal, 1st Railway Gate, Sandur, Ballari due to rash and negligent driving of Innova Car bearing Reg.

2 No.KA-22-AA-2238 dashed against the SCCH-5 petitioner motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2.

3. What order or award?
6.

In order to prove the case, Petitioner himself examined as PW-1, examined Dr.Shailesh A.V.Rao,
Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics as PW-2 and marked 20 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record and my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the SCCH-5 following:
::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove the case, petitioner examined himself as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated.

In order to prove road traffic accident PW-1 produced and marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint as Ex.P.2,
copy of spot mahazar as Ex.P.3, copy of seizure mahazar as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report as Ex.P.5,
copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.7.
9.
Further to substantiate the petitioner's case, petitioner has examined Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1, PW-2 and documents those have marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 corroborates the case of the SCCH-5 petitioner about occurrence of the road traffic accident dated 20.12.2023 as alleged in the petition.

10. Per contra, except filing of written statement, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and to discard the evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, this tribunal held that the petitioner sustained the injuries due to the accident occurred on 20.12.2023 at about 4.10 p.m. when he was riding Scooty bearing Reg. No.KA- 35-EN-9779 near Thoranagal 1st Railway Gate, Sandu,
Ballari District.
11. It is evident from police papers that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of driver of the Innova Car bearing Reg. No.KA-22-AA-2238.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this SCCH-5 tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained right fronto temporo parietal acute subdural hematoma and subarachnoid hemorrhage, for the said injuries, he underwent right fronto temporo parietal decompressive craniotomy and evacuation of subdural hematoma.
Further he underwent titanium mesh cranioplasty and reexploration, redo craniplasty and subgaleo peritoneal shunt.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.6,
discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by Fortis Hospital wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 21.12.2023 to 03.01.2024, 11.01.2024 to 15.01.2024, 24.01.2024 to 26.01.2024,
thereafter from SCCH-5 01.02.2024 to 05.02.2024.

Further he has exhibited taxi bill of Rs.20,000/-
marked as Ex.P.12, CT-Scan report as Ex.P.14.
13.
Further Dr.Shailes A.V.Rao is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited xxx and he has assessed permanent physical disability of OPD Record as Ex.P.15, mini mental state examination report as Ex.P.16, X-ray reports as Ex.P.17, CT-Scan report as Ex.P.18, X-ray Films as Ex.P.19 and CT-Scan as Ex.P.20. PW-2
has assessed neuro disability pertaining to cognition, which amounts to disability around 15%.
the disability pertains to whole body is likely to be permanent.

In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner and he has not taken any opinion from the treated Doctors and he has verified discharge summary SCCH-5 of Fortis Hospital and psychological assessment of NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru and OPD records of Narayana Hrudayalaya Hospital.
Further PW-2 deposed that, right fronto parietal decompressive now became normal and appearance is normal, but internal scarring of brain is present.
Further deposed that, petitioner is capable of taking day to day personal care and hygiene and he can identify his family members and to some extent the petitioner can manage with strangers.
The minimum MMSC score is 25, the petitioner's score is below average.
Further he has not obtained opinion of Neuro Psychologist and he has assessed the disability on 2001 and 2018 guidelines.
PW-2 deposed that, he is not a member of any Medical Board and petitioner is capable of identifying things around him.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries SCCH-5 sustained by the petitioner the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 15%
for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

14. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 64 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.13, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 06.11.1959 and the alleged accident is occurred on 20.12.2023, accordingly relying on Ex.P.13 his age is considered about 64 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 7 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8, petitioner took treatment as inpatient for 23 days.

As per the evidence of PW-2 he examined petitioner on 13.08.2025 after 1 year 8 months and as per version of PW-2 and by considering the gravity SCCH-5 of injury sustained by petitioner it may take at least three months to heal the wound.
For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income.

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.48,000/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
17. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.11 medical bills for Rs.3,08,731/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is concerned.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.6 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the SCCH-5 accident caused on 20.10.2023.
So as per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained injuries over right tempo parietal region which are grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Manjunatha for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
18.
Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

1. Loss of Future Income 2,01,600-00 2.
Pain and sufferings 25,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 3,08,731-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 SCCH-5 6. Loss of income during laid up 48,000-00 period Total 6,13,331-00 19.

Accordingly this tribunal hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,13,331/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

20. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.TBA/50204752 which is valid for the period from 25.04.2023 to 24.04.2024, the alleged Nagaraju B vs Shruti Darshan Patil on 29 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39828244/

21. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,13,331/- (Rupees six lakhs thirteen thousand three hundred thirty one only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept SCCH-5 in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
